### The Weight of Law

When the old [czar]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="czar · n. 沙皇，皇帝；独裁者"}'s only [heir]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="heir · n. 继承人"} refused to [comply]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="comply · vi. 答应；遵守；顺从，遵从"} with a tribunal summons, the case spiraled fast. The [felon]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="felon · n. 重罪犯; 瘭疽,甲沟炎,指头脓炎; 残忍的,残暴的,邪恶的"} had been caught running a scheme that touched every layer of the state: he had **levied** illegal fees on merchants, invoked a forged [lien]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="lien · n. 留置权；抵押品所产生的利息"} against a rival's property, and spread [libel]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="libel · n. 诽谤罪；诋毁；毁坏名誉的东西；控诉书; 对…进行诽谤；中伤；控告; 进行文字诽谤"} about the city's chief [consul]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="consul · n. 领事"}. The local [civic]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="civic · adj. 城市的; 公民的,市民的"} court issued a [caveat]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="caveat · n. 警告；中止诉讼手续的申请；货物出门概不退换；停止支付的广告"} before proceeding, wary of political blowback.

A government [bureau]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="bureau · n. 衣柜；局，处；办公桌"} opened an investigation. Its mandate was clear: examine every [tort]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="tort · n. 侵权行为"} committed under the former regime, during the years the strongman had [reigned]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="reign · vi. 统治；盛行；支配；君临; 统治；支配；统治时期"} unchallenged. A new set of [bylaws]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="bylaws · n. 章程；规章制度；细则"} had already been [enacted]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="enact · vt. 制定；通过"} to close the loopholes through which so many [torts]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="torts · n. 侵权行为"} had slipped. Prosecutors moved to [evict]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="evict · v. 驱逐，赶出，逐出"} the defendants from their offices and had three of them sent to [jail]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="jail · n. 监狱；监牢；拘留所; 监禁；下狱"} pending trial. The charges were strictly [penal]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="penal · adj. 刑事的；刑罚的"} — the [parol]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="parol · adj. 口头的；没有签章的; 口头言词；口头答辩；石蜡燃料"} agreements they had relied on carried no weight once the written evidence surfaced.

A foreign [envoy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="envoy · n. 使者；全权公使"} arrived to observe the proceedings, accompanied by a [proxy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="proxy · n. 代表权；代理权；代理人，代表 Proxy代理服务器，即Proxy服务器，在互联网上的完成跑腿服务。当…"} from an allied nation. Outside the courtroom, a well-funded [lobby]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="lobby · n. 前厅, 厅堂; 议会休息室; 游说议员的团体; &amp; 向…进行游说"} group worked the corridors, trying to water down a key [clause]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="clause · n. 从句; 条款"} in the upcoming statute — the one that would make certain conduct [licit]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="licit · adj. 合法的,准许的"} only with full parliamentary approval. The [curfew]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="curfew · n. 宵禁；宵禁令；晚钟；打晚钟时刻"} imposed on the capital kept the crowds thin, but it did nothing to stop the debate. Inside the chamber, a [censor]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="censor · vt. 审查，检查; 检查员；潜意识压抑力；信件检查员"} reviewed transcripts for anything that might inflame the public, while defense attorneys prepared to [accuse]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="accuse · v. 控告；控诉；谴责；归咎于"} the prosecution of overreach. The state's power had been [curbed]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="curbed · adj. 约束的; 约束；抑制"} before; whether the new law would hold was a question no one could yet answer.

### A Constitutional Crisis, Gavel by Gavel

The [borough]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="borough · n. 区；自治的市镇"} council had long been a quiet institution, but the morning the governor issued an emergency [decree]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="decree · n. 法令；判决; 颁布；命令；判决；注定; 发布命令；注定"} suspending local elections, every clerk, [notary]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="notary · n. 公证人"}, and [deputy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="deputy · n. 代理人，代表; 副的；代理的"} in City Hall knew the old order was finished. Protesters gathered on the courthouse steps, waving placards that read: *No [tyrant]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="tyrant · n. 专制统治者；暴君; 暴君似的人；专横的人; 严酷的事物，苛刻的事物; 僭主，僭王"} rules a free people*. Inside, attorneys scrambled to [indict]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="indict · vt. 控告, 起诉"} the administration's senior officials, arguing the governor had tried to [impute]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="impute · vt. 归罪于，归咎于；嫁祸于"} criminal motive to peaceful demonstrators and [impose]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="impose · vi. 欺骗；利用；施加影响; 强加；以…欺骗；征税"} an illegal curfew. The presiding judge, reviewing the [docket]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="docket · n. 摘要；记事表；诉讼事件表; 在...上附加摘要"} page by page, agreed: she would neither [revoke]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="revoke · vt. 撤销, 取消, 废除"} the citizens' right to assembly nor allow the state to [pledge]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="pledge · n. 抵押；保证，誓言；抵押品，典当物; 保证，许诺；用……抵押；举杯祝……健康"} civil liberties away in exchange for a hollow promise of order.

---

By afternoon the hearings had spilled into federal court. The question before the bench was whether the governor's office could be held [liable]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="liable · adj. 有法律责任的, 有义务的; 易患…的, 易受…之害的; 有做某事的倾向"} for the [alleged]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="alleged · adj. 声称的,所谓的"} seizure of protest funds held in [escrow]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="escrow · n. 由第三者保存附带条件委付盖印的契约"} by a neutral bank. Defense counsel invoked the [feudal]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="feudal · adj. 封建的"} logic of executive supremacy — that every power flowed downward from the throne of the [empire]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="empire · n. 帝国；帝王统治，君权"} — but the presiding panel was unmoved. [Hereby]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="hereby · adv. 以此方式，据此；特此"} and henceforth, the judges wrote in their ruling, such reasoning belonged in a history archive, not a modern courtroom. They moved to [uphold]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="uphold · vt. 赞成；支撑；鼓励；举起"} the lower court's finding and ordered the funds released, noting that [equity]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="equity · n. 公平，公正；普通股；衡平法；抵押资产的净值"} demanded no less.

---

The crisis eventually forced the legislature to act. Several breakaway [states]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="states · n. 州，国家; 陈述；声明"} threatened to [secede]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="secede · vi. 退出；脱离; 从…中脱离；割让"} from the federation unless a new [treaty]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="treaty · n. 条约，协议；谈判"} of shared governance was signed within thirty days. Hardliners demanded [amnesty]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="amnesty · n. 大赦，特赦; 对…实行大赦"} for officials who had acted under orders; civil-rights groups insisted every [felony]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="felony · n. 重罪"} charge remain intact. A special mediator was appointed to manage the competing demands: she carried a [legacy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="legacy · n. 遗产, 遗赠物; 遗留之物"} of brokering impossible deals, once shepherding a landmark [zoning]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="zoning · n. 分区制；都市的区域划分"} reform through a capital gridlocked for a decade. Her first act was to [ratify]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="ratify · vt. 批准；认可"} a temporary ceasefire in the litigation. Her second was to place the most contentious documents under [remand]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="remand · n. 还押；送还，遣回; 还押，还押候审；遣回"}, freezing them from further appeal while negotiations ran. A divorce lawyer in the gallery — there on an [alimony]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="alimony · n. 赡养费,生活费"} dispute that had been pushed back three weeks — muttered that the whole spectacle proved governments were just very expensive family feuds. The mediator's office chose not to [impute]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="impute · vt. 归罪于，归咎于；嫁祸于"} any particular meaning to that observation. They simply moved to [abolish]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="abolish · vt. 废除, 废止"} the disputed emergency powers by statute, before any [secede]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="secede · vi. 退出；脱离; 从…中脱离；割让"}-minded faction could turn threat into reality.

### The Trial That Shook the Republic

The [Capitol]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Capitol · n. 美国国会大厦；州议会大厦"} had seen tense sessions before, but nothing quite like this. The [cabinet]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="cabinet · n. 内阁；橱柜；展览艺术品的小陈列室; 内阁的；私下的，秘密的"} convened in emergency, its members speaking in hushed, almost secretive tones. At the center of the storm was a senior [nominee]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="nominee · n. 被任命者；被提名的人；代名人"} to the Federal Bench—a man who had, according to prosecutors, operated far beyond the [confines]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="confine · n. 界限，边界; 限制；禁闭"} of his authority.

The lead [counsel]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="counsel · n. 忠告；讨论；商议；决策；法律顾问; 劝告；建议; 提出忠告；商讨"} for the prosecution rose and addressed the chamber. The [sheriff]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="sheriff · n. 县的司法长官"} had already [impounded]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="impound · vt. 依法没收, 扣押; 将暂存待领"} the defendant's files; [customs]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="customs · n. 海关；关税；习惯；风俗"} agents had flagged irregular wire transfers at the border. The charge was stark: the official had [imposed]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="imposed · adj. 强加的；施加的；应用的; 把…强加于；欺骗"} unlawful duties without [consent]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="consent · n. 准许，同意，赞成; 同意；赞成"} of the legislature, [forfeiting]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="forfeit · n. 罚金；没收物；丧失的东西; 因受罚而丧失的；被没收的; 丧失"} any claim to public trust. The defense [pleaded]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="pleaded · v. 辩护"} mitigating circumstances and **justified** each decision as an act of [command]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="command · vi. 命令，指挥；控制; 命令，指挥；控制；远望; 命令；司令部；指挥，控制"} during a national emergency—but the committee was unmoved. A motion to [impeach]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="impeach · vt. 控告犯罪，弹劾；怀疑，提出异议"} passed along party lines. The presiding officer moved to [suspend]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="suspend · vt. 延缓，推迟；使暂停；使悬浮; 悬浮；禁赛"} his duties pending full review, and a [recusal]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="recusal · n. 宣布不合格,取消资格"} was demanded from every judge with a prior personal relationship to the accused.

Outside the hearing room, political theorists debated the deeper currents. A professor of [Marxism]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Marxism · n. 马克思主义; 马克思的；马克思主义的"} argued that the episode merely exposed contradictions inherent in [monarch]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="monarch · n. 君主, 帝王"}-derived legal traditions never fully purged from the republic's DNA—relics of [emperor]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="emperor · n. 皇帝，君主"} and [empress]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="empress · n. 女皇; 皇后"}, of [regency]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="regency · n. 摄政；摄政统治；摄政权"} councils and [serfdom]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="serfdom · n. 农奴境遇；农奴身份"}, still haunting modern [statute]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="statute · n. 法令, 法规"} books. A colleague countered that the written [mandate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="mandate · n. 授权; 正式命令; 将委托某国管理; 授权根据委托统治权"} of the constitution, properly read, [entitled]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="entitle · vt. 称做…；定名为…；给…称号；使…有权利"} citizens to far stronger protections. A veteran [referee]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="referee · n. 裁判员；调解人；介绍人; 担任裁判；仲裁; 为…当裁判；调停"} of constitutional disputes—summoned to [preside]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="preside · vi. 主持，担任会议主席; 管理"} over the panel—noted wryly that every side [pledged]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="pledged · v. 保证；抵押；给予"} fidelity to the law while bending it to convenience. The child-[custody]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="custody · n. 保管；拘留；监护；抚养权"} dispute between the state and the defendant's family over sealed documents added yet another layer of drama; the records remained in the [custody]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="custody · n. 保管；拘留；监护；抚养权"} of the court clerk until further order.

By evening, the [Capitol]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Capitol · n. 美国国会大厦；州议会大厦"} dome glowed against a grey sky. Whatever verdict came, the republic had been reminded that no office, however grand, sits beyond the reach of its own foundational rules.

### The Trial That Shook the Republic

The old **mandate** had collapsed. In the capital's grand courthouse, a [forensic]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="forensic · adj. 辩论的；法院的；适于法庭的"} team spent weeks assembling evidence against the former [dictator]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="dictator · n. 独裁者；命令者"}, whose [imperial]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="imperial · adj. 皇帝的；帝国的；威严的；至高无上的; 纸张尺寸；特等品"} ambitions had long threatened the fragile [autonomy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="autonomy · n. 自治，自治权"} of the southern provinces. Citizens who had once lived under a suffocating [hegemony]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="hegemony · n. 霸权；领导权；盟主权"} now watched the proceedings with cautious hope. The [partisan]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="partisan · adj. 偏袒的；党派的；盲目推崇的；效忠的; 游击队；虔诚信徒；党羽"} press ran headlines daily. Outside, a [tribune]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="tribune · n. 护民官；讲坛；看台；公民权利保护者"} mounted a temporary platform and read aloud the charges to the crowd, his voice steady despite the hecklers. The defense chose to [disclaim]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="disclaim · vt. 拒绝承认；放弃，弃权；否认，拒绝; 否认；放弃；弃权"} any connection between their client and the seized documents — documents that [attested]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="attested · adj. 证明无病的；经检验证明无病的；经检验证明无菌的"} to a conspiracy stretching back decades.

Inside, the chief [delegate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="delegate · n. 代表；会议代表; 授；把委托; 选派"} from the eastern federation presented the [covenant]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="covenant · n. 契约，盟约；盖印合同；圣约; 订立盟约、契约; 立约承诺"} signed by three regional governments, arguing it stripped the accused of any claim to sovereign immunity. The prosecution's [advocacy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="advocacy · n. 拥护；主张；辩护"} was relentless: the defendant was [culpable]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="culpable · adj. 有罪的；该责备的；不周到的；应受处罚的"}, [entitled]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="entitled · adj. 题名为，书名叫做… ；有资格的"} to no [leniency]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="leniency · n. 宽大;仁慈"} given the scale of the scheme. A doctrine of [estoppel]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="estoppel · n. 禁止反言,禁止,防止"} barred him from now denying statements his own ministers had made on the record. When the jury returned, the [verdict]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="verdict · n. 裁决, 裁定; 决定, 意见"} was guilty on all counts — [treason]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="treason · n. 叛国罪；不忠"} among them. The judge declined to [nominate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="nominate · vt. 提名；任命；指定；推荐"} a lenient sentence; the [guaranty]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="guaranty · n. 保证,保证书,担保物,抵押物; 保证,抵押,担保"} of equal justice, she said, demanded otherwise. No [warrant]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="warrant · n. 授权证；许可证; 使…显得合理；成为…的根据; 保证，担保"} existed to soften what the law required.

The aftermath rippled outward. The new coalition moved quickly to [federate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="federate · vt. &amp; 结成联邦"} the remaining city-states under a reformed charter, determined to [liberate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="liberate · vt. 解放；释放；放出"} governance from the grip of personal rule. A senior [mandarin]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="mandarin · n. 官话; 中国政府的高级官员"} in the justice ministry quietly arranged the transfer of the convicted man's estate, noting that under existing [tenancy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="tenancy · n. 租用, 租赁; 租用或租赁期"} law his family could keep the house — provided they did not contest the asset freeze. Historians would later recall the episode as the moment the old [monarchy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="monarchy · n. 君主统治, 君主制度; 君主国"} truly ended, the day a [Peronist]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Peronist · adj. 庇隆主义的；庇隆主义者的"}-style strongman learned that no amount of [mistrial]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="mistrial · n. 无效审判"} motions could indefinitely delay accountability.

### The Trial That Shook the State

The [inaugural]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="inaugural · adj. 就职的, 就任的"} session of the newly formed [appellate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="appellate · adj. 上诉的; 受理上诉的"} court opened under heavy scrutiny. The [reigning]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="reigning · adj. 统治的；在位的；本届的；起支配作用的; 统治；支配；盛行"} administration had long operated as a near-[autocracy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="autocracy · n. 独裁；独裁统治；独裁政体; 独裁政府;独裁统治的国家"}, and reformers hoped this case would begin to dismantle that order. The [defendant]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="defendant · n. 被告"}, a former minister accused of [tortious]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="tortious · adj. 侵权行为的，非法行为的"} conduct and deliberate misuse of public funds, entered the chamber flanked by his [trustees]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="trustees · n. 受托人，受托者"}. His lawyers had already filed an [affidavit]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="affidavit · n. 宣誓书,书面陈述"} denying every charge, yet the prosecution argued that [scienter]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="scienter · n. 明知；故意"} — the minister's full knowledge of the scheme — was beyond dispute.

The [appellant]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="appellant · n. 上诉人"} in a parallel civil suit arrived carrying a stack of documents: an [amendment]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="amendment · n. 修改，改动；修正案"} to the original contract, a [subpoena]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="subpoena · n. 传票; 传唤"} served to three senior officials, and a [concordat]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="concordat · n. 协定；宗派间的协约"} the government had quietly signed with a foreign [consulate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="consulate · n. 领事馆"} to [extradite]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="extradite · vt. 引渡"} a key witness. [Pursuant]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="pursuant · adj. 依据的；追赶的；随后的; 依照；根据"} to standing court [protocol]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="protocol · n. 礼仪；外交礼仪; 草案，草约；议定的条款，议定书"}, all materials were logged before proceedings began. The [incumbent]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="incumbent · adj. 在职的; 义不容辞的; 教区牧师; 教会中的任职者 Incumbent传统运营商"} minister had governed for two decades, so when the [allegation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="allegation · n. 说法，指控"} surfaced — that his office had orchestrated the quiet [annexation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="annexation · n. 并吞；附加；附加物"} of protected state land — the capital was caught off guard. The [paralegal]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="paralegal · adj. 辅助律师业务的; 律师的专职助手,律师帮办"} team worked through the night assembling evidence, careful to flag every document marked [classified]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="classified · adj. 归入密级的,保密的"}.

Yet the judge found the [testimony]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="testimony · n. 证词; 证明, 证据"} of a former aide far more persuasive: she described a backroom [concession]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="concession · n. 承认, 允许; 妥协, 让步; 特许权"} in which civil servants were told to ignore [de minimis]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="de minimis"} violations without reporting them.

The opposition bloc chose [abstention]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="abstention · n. 戒除；避免; 弃权; 戒绝者；弃权者"} rather than a formal vote of no confidence, wary of the precedent. It sought a full [conviction]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="conviction · n. 确信, 坚定的信仰; 定罪, 判罪"}, arguing that only a clear [warranted]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="warranted · adj. 担保的，保证的"} penalty — not mere [probation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="probation · n. 缓刑, 察看; 试用, 试读"} — would deter future abuse. Separate civil proceedings asked the court to [indemnify]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="indemnify · vt. 保障,保护; 使免于受罚; 补偿,赔偿"} all displaced residents and to draw up an [indemnity]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="indemnity · n. 保障, 赔偿, 补偿; 赔款, 补偿金, 赔偿物"} schedule backed by [Dodd-Frank]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Dodd-Frank"}-style financial rules that would force the ministry to post bond.

### The Weight of the State

When the **legislature** convenes, the air inside [parliament]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="parliament · n. 议会, 国会"} always carries a faint tension — part theater, part genuine contest of will. In the gallery sat the [petitioner]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="petitioner · n. 请求人;请愿人; 离婚案原告"} in a separate civil case, quietly grateful that [arbitration]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="arbitration · n. 仲裁；公断"} had spared her years of open [litigation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="litigation · n. 打官司; 诉讼"}. She knew she was [accountable]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="accountable · adj. 负有责任的, 应对自己的行为做出说明的"} for what she did next, and that her professional [credentials]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="credentials · n. 资格证书; 国书; 证书; 资格"} would either protect her or mark her as a target. The scandal, legal analysts noted, could [account for]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="account for 对…负有责任；对…做出解释；说明……的原因"} the ruling party's collapse in the polls — a minor [peccadillo]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="peccadillo · n. 轻罪,小过失"} at the start, now a full [indictment]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="indictment · n. 衰败迹象，腐败迹象; 刑事起诉书；公诉书; 控告；起诉"} of an entire system's failure to hold power [accountable]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="accountable · adj. 负有责任的, 应对自己的行为做出说明的"}. ### The Making of a Government

The [inauguration]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="inauguration · n. 就职;就职典礼; 开始;开创; 开幕;落成"} was supposed to signal a new era. Standing before his [constituency]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="constituency · n. 选区的）选民；支持者；顾客"}, the newly elected president spoke of [unalienable]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="unalienable · adj. 不能让与的,不能剥夺的"} rights and promised to dismantle every [bureaucratic]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="bureaucratic · adj. 官僚的, 官僚主义的, 官僚作风的"} obstacle that had calcified over decades of [dictatorship]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="dictatorship · n. 独裁;专政; 独裁统治的国家"}. The old regime had ruled [unilaterally]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="unilaterally · adv. 单方面地"}, treating the state's [prerogative]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="prerogative · n. 权利,特权; 大主教法庭; 总督委任组成的法庭"} as personal property, and its collapse had left a vacuum: courts without clear [jurisdiction]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="jurisdiction · n. 司法权; 裁判权"}, a gutted [secretariat]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="secretariat · n. 秘书处, 书记处"}, and a [kommandatura]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="kommandatura · n. 军事管制总部"} still nominally overseeing three disputed border districts under a crumbling [multilateral]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="multilateral · adj. 多方面的;多边的; 多边贸易; 多方面地;多边地"} agreement no one had bothered to revoke.

The transitional assembly moved fast. [Legislative]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="legislative · adj. 立法的"} committees drafted new statutes, and the [codification]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="codification · n. 法典编纂,法律成文化"} of civil liberties — once an [abolitionist]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="abolitionist · n. 废除主义者；废奴主义者; 废除主义者的；主张废除主义的; 已废除死刑的"} dream — was finally put to paper. A [nonpartisan]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="nonpartisan · adj. 无党无派的,超乎党派的"} commission was empaneled to oversee [ratification]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="ratification · n. 正式批准;认可"} of the new constitution, and a separate tribunal began cataloguing every [infringement]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="infringement · n. 违反; 侵犯,伤害"} of rights under the old order. Victims sought [restitution]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="restitution · n. 归还原主, 恢复原状; 赔偿, 补偿"} for seized property, while advocacy groups pushed for broader [reparations]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="reparations · n. 赔款"} to communities destroyed by forced labour. The harder cases went to appeal; courts quietly debated [appealability]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="appealability · n. 可上诉性"} standards for crimes the prior code had never named. Where clear guilt was established, [retribution]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="retribution · n. 应得的惩罚或赔偿"} was meant to be proportional — judges were warned against [malpractice]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="malpractice · n. 玩忽职守, 渎职, 不法行为"} born of political pressure. [Notarization]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="notarization · n. 公证"} requirements were overhauled so that ordinary citizens, not just party loyalists, could authenticate documents. The [protectorate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="protectorate · n. 保护国；摄政政体；摄政职位；摄政任期"} arrangement with two smaller neighbours was renegotiated; both sides agreed that the old [prescriptive]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="prescriptive · adj. 规定的, 指定的, 制定的; 约定俗成的, 惯例的"} rules, inherited from a colonial compact, no longer reflected reality.

The hardest fight was over the economy. Industry lobbies celebrated [deregulation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="deregulation · n. 违反规定,反常"} as freedom; unions called it a licence for exploitation. Every [municipality]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="municipality · n. 自治市; 自治区; 自治市或区的政府当局"} from the capital to the remotest hill town held public hearings. International observers argued for [accreditation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="accreditation · n. 委派,信赖,鉴定合格"} of independent audit bodies before foreign aid could flow. One coalition threatened to [rubber-stamp]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="rubber-stamp · vt. 不经审查就批准"} nothing until [emancipation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="emancipation · n. 解放"}-era property claims — long buried in administrative backlog — were resolved. In the end, a [multilateral]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="multilateral · adj. 多方面的;多边的; 多边贸易; 多方面地;多边地"} oversight board was seated, its mandate narrow and its patience short. Whether it would amount to anything more than another layer of [bureaucratic]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="bureaucratic · adj. 官僚的, 官僚主义的, 官僚作风的"} delay, no one yet knew.

### The Long Arc of Reform

The young republic had begun as a loose [confederation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="confederation · n. 联盟；同盟；邦联"} of city-states, each jealous of its sovereignty, each suspicious of the center. Over generations, however, the pressure of [decolonization]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="decolonization · n. 非殖民化"} reshaped the political landscape: former territories demanded full membership, and the old [imperialistic]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="imperialistic · adj. 帝国主义的,帝制的"} hierarchies could no longer hold. A wave of constitutional amendments swept through parliament, and [desegregation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="desegregation · n. 废除种族隔离"} of public institutions — schools, courts, housing registries — was written into law. [Discriminatory]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="discriminatory · adj. 有识别力的; 差别对待的"} hiring practices that had persisted for decades were finally subject to judicial review, and employers who ignored the new statutes faced [nullification]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="nullification · n. 无效,废弃,取消,使无价值,使变的无用"} of their operating licenses.

The reform coalition was not without its fractures. A faction of [Marxist-Leninist]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Marxist-Leninist · adj. 马克思列宁主义的"} delegates pushed for collective ownership of the press; moderates countered that a free press was the only guarantee of genuine [accountability]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="accountability · n. 有责任,有义务,可说明性"} in an [administrative]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="administrative · adj. 行政的，管理的；经营的; 后方勤务的"} state. After months of procedural wrangling, a veteran [parliamentarian]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="parliamentarian · n. 议事法规专家,国会议员; 议会的"} broke the deadlock by invoking an obscure standing rule, forcing the chamber to a vote. The motion passed narrowly, and with it came a landmark [indemnification]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="indemnification · n. 赔偿;保障; 赔偿物"} fund for citizens whose property had been seized without due process under the old regime. Those who had suffered under [incarceration]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="incarceration · n. 钳闭"} orders issued by emergency tribunals — orders now declared void — could file claims through a new [unincorporated]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="unincorporated · adj. 未组成社团的;未被承认为自治组织的;未包含在内的"} relief board, a body that sat outside the normal civil-service hierarchy precisely to avoid conflicts of interest.

The closing months of the reform era were consumed by a single, divisive case. A former security minister, rather than fight extradition, chose to [turn myself in]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="turn myself in"} — surrendering at the border checkpoint at dawn. His legal team immediately moved to [appeal the verdict]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="appeal the verdict"} handed down by the lower tribunal, citing violations of the [parol evidence rule]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="parol evidence rule 口头证据规则；排斥外在证据原则 Parol Evidence Rule证言规则"}: prosecutors had introduced recorded conversations that, the defense argued, contradicted the plain text of a signed agreement and should have been excluded. The government's lead counsel issued a formal [disclaimation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="disclaimation · n. 弃权,否认"} of any intent to prosecute selectively, and invoked the doctrine of [nonrepudiation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="nonrepudiation 认可"} — the digital signature on the ministerial order, she argued, bound its author irrevocably. The case dragged on for two years, but its outcome mattered less, in the end, than what it proved: that the machinery of accountability, however slow, had begun to turn.
